About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Visual Arts – Design Years 12–
13 of the New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Visual Arts – Design Years 12–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Visual Arts – Design Years 12–13 is proposed
to be made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under
section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Visual Arts – Design Years 12–13 will be required to start using it in Year 12
from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred




Visual Arts – Design | Years 12–13 | October 2026                                          Page 2

Purpose statement
                                                                    Te toi whakairo, ka ihiihi, ka wehiwehi, ka aweawe   Artistic excellence makes the world sit up in wonder.
                                                                    te ao katoa.




  In Visual Arts – Design, students are taught how visual communication, design
  processes, and visual language are used to create purposeful design. Students
  learn to investigate, develop, and refine ideas in response to a design proposition
  across a range of contexts, including print, digital media, and illustration. Through
  iteration, students use drawing methods, typography, layout, imagery, and
  technologies to communicate effectively with an intended audience.


Students are taught key design concepts and practices and research how designers
respond to purpose, audience, and context. They examine a range of contexts,
including cultural, social, historical, and contemporary perspectives, to understand
how meaning is constructed and communicated through design and how design
reflects different viewpoints and values.

Design provides students with the knowledge and practices to investigate, analyse,
evaluate, and apply understanding through design-making. This disciplinary
knowledge supports students to generate, refine, and present purposeful resolved
design, develop confidence communicating ideas, respond to audiences, and
consider the influence of context on visual communication.

As students progress through Years 12 and 13, they develop technical, conceptual,
and contextual knowledge through explorative and sustained design practice. This
enables them to make informed design decisions and communicate ideas effectively.
They increasingly work independently to refine and realise ethical, culturally
responsive design informed by contemporary contexts.

  Visual Arts – Design leads to pathways in creative industries and related fields
  such as graphic design, advertising, digital media, user experience (UX) design,
  branding, and visual communication.

 Disciplinary Writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within the discipline.

 In Visual Arts – Design, students use explicitly taught disciplinary writing to analyse established practice and communicate the creative ideas, processes, intentions, and meanings in own and others’
 designs.

 Responsible use of artificial intelligence
 Artificial intelligence (AI) can support learning, research, inquiry, and creative processes, but it may also introduce bias, inaccuracies, ethical concerns, and issues relating to
 ownership. AI should enhance, not replace, critical or creative thinking, source evaluation, subject knowledge, or students’ own analysis and decision-making. Responsible AI use
 emphasises the importance of exercising independent judgement, drawing on credible sources, verifying information, being transparent about AI use, considering diverse
 perspectives, and developing independent thinking.
